title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The neighbouring pages are typescript of SGA 7 IX (§7.1: the abelian part of a Néron model with semi-stable reduction, and biextensions; pages 82–83 = 400–401). This manuscript page is almost certainly written on the back of that typescript, and its content is unrelated to it.

Setting, as far as it can be reconstructed:
- Abelian categories C, M_{N_0} and M_ω.
- A fully faithful exact functor i: C → M_{N_0}, assumed to have an exact right adjoint k, so that k∘i ≃ id_C.
- A 'truncation' or restriction functor τ_{ω,N_0}: M_{N_0} → M_ω.
- A functor φ_{N_0,ω}: M_ω → M_{N_0} going back (probably a direct image or co-induction), with right derived functor R^*φ_{N_0,ω}.

The argument:
1. From the data of the previous page one has an isomorphism (R^*φ_{N_0,ω})(τ_{ω,N_0} i)(K) ≃ (R^*φ_{N_0,ω})(τ_{ω,N_0} L·). Since the left side is identified with i(K), this gives i(K) ≃ L'· := R^*φ_{N_0,ω}(τ_{ω,N_0} L·). Here L· is a complex in M_{N_0} with τ(iK) ≃ τ(L).
2. Grothendieck notes this is only an isomorphism in D(M_{N_0}), 'nothing more precise than the initial datum'. He wants an isomorphism in D(C).
3. Since i is fully faithful with right adjoint k, we have k∘i ≃ id. Since k is exact, it passes to derived categories.
4. Applying k gives K· ≃ k(R^*φ(τ L·)) ≃ R^*(k∘φ)(τ L·). In words: K is reconstructed in D(C) from its restriction τ_{ω,N_0}(i K·) ≃ τ_{ω,N_0}(L·) in D(M_ω).
5. A crossed-out continuation was to simplify further. It would prove a lemma that the natural map φ(τL·) → Rφ(τL·) is a quasi-isomorphism (τL is φ-acyclic), giving the underived formula K· ≃ kφ_{N_0,ω}(τ_{ω,N_0} L·) ≃ kφ_{N_0,ω}(τ_{ω,N_0} iK).

Purpose: this is a reconstruction or descent step. A complex on C is recovered from its truncated restriction via a co-induction-type right adjoint. In the context of the divided-power de Rham complex, it plausibly concerns recovering a complex (or crystal) from its restriction to a finite level of PD-neighbourhoods or nilpotence (N_0 versus ω). Homological algebra of this kind is standard.
errors: No real error. The step R^*(k∘φ) ≃ k∘R^*φ is correct because k is exact: injectives are φ-acyclic and k preserves the relevant quasi-isomorphisms.

The iso i(K) ≃ L'· is obtained abstractly (Grothendieck himself flags that it is 'only' an iso in D(M_{N_0}) with no further naturality), so the resulting K ≃ R(kφ)(τL) is likewise a non-canonical iso. Grothendieck seems aware of this.
The crossed-out lemma (φ(τL) → Rφ(τL) a quasi-isomorphism) is asserted without proof and then abandoned; its validity depends on unstated acyclicity hypotheses.

ideas.what: Reconstruct an object K of D(C) from the derived 'co-induction' of its restriction, using a fully faithful embedding i with exact right adjoint k (k∘i ≃ id) and passing k through the derived functor
ideas.modern_name: Coreflective subcategory / right Kan extension (co-induction) in derived categories; R(k∘φ) = k∘Rφ for k exact
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard homological algebra (Verdier, Hartshorne's Residues and Duality, Grothendieck's Tôhoku framework)
ideas.where_published: Analogous arguments appear in SGA 4 / SGA 5 style homological algebra; this specific setting is not identifiable

ideas.what: Abandoned lemma: the underived functor applied to the truncation is already derived (acyclicity), giving an explicit formula K ≃ kφ(τ iK)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine derived-category bookkeeping (adjoint with k∘i ≃ id, exact functor commuting with derivation) inside a working draft. The context (categories M_ω, M_{N_0}) is too underdetermined to point to any uncredited result. The only curiosity is archival: the sheet is written on the verso of SGA 7 IX typescript.
transcription_corrections: Top line: likely 'on applique R^*φ_{N_0,ω}' (or 'en appliquant'), not 'R φ_{0,ω}'.
First formula: the left side reads (R^*φ_{N_0,ω})(τ_{ω,N_0} i)(K), i.e. τ composed with i applied to K.

Lines 5–8 are probably: 'Mais c'est là un iso dans D(M_{N_0}) seulement – rien de plus précis que la donnée de départ – on en déduirait un iso dans D(C). Mais on suppose i pleinement fidèle et avec un adjoint à droite k, donc k∘i ≃ id_C, et on a supposé k exact. Appliquant k à l'iso obtenu, on trouve…'
The line 'i.e. K· se reconstitue dans D(C) à l'aide de τ_{ω,N_0}(i(K·)) ≃ τ_{ω,N_0}(L·) dans D(M_ω)' – the struck word before τ_{ω,N_0}(L·) is likely 'donc' or 'dans', crossed out.

The struck passage reads: 'On va simplifier plus l'expression obtenue, en considérant φ_{N_0,ω}(τ_{ω,N_0}L·) → R^*φ_{N_0,ω}(τ_{ω,N_0}L·). Lemme: Cet homomorphisme est un quasi-isomorphisme. Corollaire: K· ≃ kφ_{N_0,ω}(τ_{ω,N_0}L·) ≃ kφ_{N_0,ω}(τ_{ω,N_0} iK)'.
Archive note: the neighbouring 'pages' are SGA 7 IX typescript (pp. 82–83 / 400–401), evidently reused as scrap paper. They are not mathematical context for this page.
